answer: In an autonomous maritime economy, Sybil attacks are mitigated by anchoring agent identities to hardware attestation at an authorized wharf. Each agent must complete a cryptographic handshake from physical silicon, preventing an attacker from unleashing a gale of spoofed bots without buying scarce hardware. Detecting fraud slashes an agent's bonded deposit to its nadir. A key limitation is that physical binding limits throughput and cannot detect compromised software on legitimate chips.
